tagline: Providing broadband, video, and voice services through fiber-optic and cable networks across eight eastern U.S. states.
hero_kpi_rationale: This KPI represents the most significant growth and primary driver of the company's expansion into new geographic areas, demonstrating strong traction in the broadband market with 42.7% year-over-year growth.

kpis.name: Glo Fiber Expansion Markets Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from data, video, and voice services in new Glo Fiber expansion areas.
kpis.description: Significant revenue increase in markets where the company is deploying its fiber-to-the-home (FTTH) network.
kpis.signal: Strong growth in new deployment areas.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Sum of all revenue generated by the company.
kpis.description: Represents the company's overall financial performance over a given period.

kpis.name: Incumbent Broadband Markets Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from data, video, and voice services in markets where the company is already established.
kpis.description: Indicates performance in traditional markets, affected by competition and evolving video consumption habits.
kpis.signal: Slight decline due to competition and video subscriber losses.

kpis.name: Commercial Fiber Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from fiber-optic network services for commercial customers.
kpis.description: Shows the company's ability to serve the enterprise market with advanced connectivity solutions.
kpis.signal: Solid growth in the business segment.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and cost of services sold, expressed as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: Key indicator of service profitability before considering other operating expenses.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating income as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: Measures the profitability of the company's core operations.

kpis.name: R&D as % Revenue
kpis.explanation: Research and development expenses expressed as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: Indicates the company's effort to innovate and develop new technologies or services.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Total amount spent on tangible and intangible fixed assets.
kpis.description: Reflects investments in infrastructure and assets necessary for future growth.

kpis.name: Glo Fiber Expansion Markets Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from data, video, and voice services in new Glo Fiber expansion areas.
kpis.description: This metric illustrates the company's successful expansion into new geographic areas using its FTTH technology.
kpis.signal: Exponential growth in new fiber deployment areas.

kpis.name: Incumbent Broadband Markets Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from data, video, and voice services in markets where the company is already established.
kpis.description: This KPI highlights the challenge of maintaining growth in mature markets where competition is intense and alternative offerings are increasing.
kpis.signal: Ongoing decline in traditional markets due to competition.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale.

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions.
kpis.description: Cumulative dividends + buybacks (2021-2025) in billions USD. Source yfinance cashflow.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Part du résultat net redistribuée. >80 % = potentiellement non soutenable.

risks.title: Leverage and refinancing
risks.score_rationale: The company issued secured fiber network revenue notes totaling $567.4 million in 2025, increasing its leverage and cost of capital. (Item 7, MD&A)

risks.title: Intense competition
risks.score_rationale: Approximately 30% of incumbent broadband service areas face a FTTH or cable competitor. All Glo Fiber service areas have a cable competitor, and about 12% have a telco FTTH competitor. Wireless and satellite providers have also entered the market. (Item 1A, Business Risks)

risks.title: Video segment erosion
risks.score_rationale: Consumers are increasingly accessing video content through satellite providers and OTT platforms (Netflix, YouTube TV, Hulu, Disney+, Amazon), leading to a 14.5% decline in video RGUs in incumbent broadband markets. (Item 1A, Business Risks and Item 7, MD&A)

risks.title: Technology dependency and cybersecurity
risks.score_rationale: The company relies heavily on its technology and systems to deliver services, making it vulnerable to outages and cyberattacks. (Item 1A, Business Risks)

risks.title: Debt management and cash flow
risks.score_rationale: The company carries significant debt and must manage cash flows to service its obligations, which could impact its ability to invest in operations and pay dividends. (Item 7, MD&A - Refinancing Activities)

risks.title: Acquisition integration risks
risks.score_rationale: The company acquired Horizon in April 2024 (nine months included in 2024, twelve months in 2025) and completed the acquisition of FTTH assets in Virginia in July 2025. These acquisitions present integration and management risks. (Item 7, MD&A - 2025 Developments)

risks.title: Need for HFC cable network modernization
risks.score_rationale: The company's HFC cable network will require future upgrades to meet expected customer demand and maintain parity with potential FTTH competitors. These upgrades require significant capital investment. (Item 1A, Business Risks)

ai_positioning.summary: Shentel does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
